content: The VAX1 (Ventral Anterior Homeobox 1) protein in humans is encoded by the VAX1 gene. This gene plays a critical role in the development of the forebrain in humans. Its presence in other species, such as mice and Xenopus frogs, indicates a conserved evolutionary function. In these organisms, the expression of VAX1 is restricted to the forebrain, as well as the optic and olfactory regions. The VAX1 gene encodes a transcription factor that contains a homeodomain located between amino acid positions 100 and 159, and an alanine-rich region between positions 216 and 253. Studies of VAX1 expression in mice have demonstrated its activity in the palate, coloboma of the visual system, the basal telencephalon, optic stalk, and visual eye fields. In these regions, VAX1 is co-expressed with the Sonic Hedgehog (Shh) and Bone Morphogenetic Protein 4 (Bmp4) genes. Clinically, homozygous mutations in the VAX1 gene in mice have been associated with craniofacial malformations, including cleft palate. Furthermore, Genome-Wide Association Studies (GWAS) have identified significant correlations between single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the VAX1 gene and non-syndromic cleft conditions in humans.
